newsitem.title: GREECE: LIANI DENIES GIVING PAPANDREOU SECRET MEDICINE.
newsitem.headline: LIANI DENIES GIVING PAPANDREOU SECRET MEDICINE.

text.p: Tales of illegal telephone taps, evil-eye spells and secret medicine at the home of late Greek prime minister Andreas Papandreou thrust his controversial widow Dimitra Liani back into the limelight on Wednesday.
A public prosecutor has opened an investigation into the phone taps while the media has devoted front pages and lengthy shows on the blonde former Olympic Airways flight attendant.

Liani, 41, confirmed published phone-tapped conversations with a homeopathic doctor and an alleged psychic, admitting she tried to get rid her ailing husband of "evil-eye spells" which were tormenting him. She denied giving him medicine secretly.
"What could I give him? There was 24-hour medical care," the controversial widow told Skai television. "I did not administer medicine. His nurses did."
She said Papandreou had tried homeopathic medicine on his own and abandoned it because it did not work for him.

His doctor and former health minister Dimitris Kremastinos said he was unaware Papandreou was taking homeopathic medicine but other doctors and family friends said it was a well-known fact in his entourage.
The wiretappings have raised questions about how Papandreou died, Liani's role in government and his medical treatment and whether the secret service was bugging the prime minister.

"We must ask how and why a European Union country stooped to being governed by an 'environment' that concealed the decay of Andreas' health and his inability to govern," wrote commentator Themos Anastasiadis in the liberal daily Eleftherotypia.
Liani testified on Tuesday before a public prosecutor investigating the wiretapping. Court sources quoted her as saying the secret service evesdropped on her.

Liani, whose meteoric rise to First Lady gained her many enemies, told Skai the published conversations dated to 1993 and 1994 after Papandreou's open-heart surgery but before his final, lengthy illness.

In one of the bugged call Liani, notoriously superstitious, asks a woman named Martha, allegedly a well-known psychic, to cast off an evil-eye spell. In another she discusses doses of homeopathic medication for Papandreou.
Liani met Papandreou in 1988 while serving him drinks on an airliner. She stood by him through election defeats, scandals and heart surgery but never gained much public sympathy.
The flamboyant socialist party founder left his American wife, Margaret, and mother of his four children to marry Liani in 1989. He was 36 years her senior.

Their public extra-marital affair was partly blamed for his 1989 election defeat after eight years in power. He weathered scandals and a tripple by-pass operation and returned to power in 1993, making Liani his chief of staff.
He was urgently hospitalised in November last year but did not resign as prime minister until two months later. He died at home in June, a day before a congress of his socialist party.
Critics accused Liani and her entourage of pumping him up to make a speech at the congress, which proved fatal. Others say no other man with Papandreou's ailments would have lived so long.

"He wanted to go (to the congress). What was my interest? To kill Papandreou?," Liani told Skai. "If he couldn't go he could send a message. I was with him body and soul." --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
